source_review: Read the complete tool() change and all five tests. Only direct TimeoutError and URLError(reason=TimeoutError) are retried, at most three total attempts; each urlopen timeout remains 120 seconds. HTTPError is a URLError with a non-timeout reason and therefore propagates immediately. Other network errors, the final timeout, and all checksum mismatches remain failures.

The fixed official URL and expected SHA-256 still come from unchanged security-tool-pins.json. Download bytes are read completely, their SHA-256 is verified, and only then is a new archive written to cache. No partial timeout or checksum-failing asset is cached. Existing cached assets are still rehashed. Archive member selection, extracted-binary comparison, supported platforms and executable permissions are unchanged.

Independent complete top-level AST comparison shows only tool() differs, plus the explicit URLError import. All parsing, scanner exit/status interpretation, severity thresholds, contextual/VEX/vendor assessments, SARIF resolution, policy load and fail-fast paths are AST-identical to the parent revision. No scanner/policy version or allowance is broadened.

Ran the actual five unittest cases locally: opened-response read timeout recovery, three-timeout exhaustion/no cache, wrapped connection timeout recovery, HTTP failure/no retry/no cache, SHA mismatch/no retry/no cache. The download boundary is simulated deliberately; this is not a successful real scanner download or a successful vulnerability scan.
